findings.description: そなたが妾と逆の目に張っているとお伝えしたら becomes After informing me that you were betting against me.

contexts.japanese:
「………ベアトも馬鹿ね。
この子はあんたのゲームであってもしっちゃかめっちゃかにするわよ」
「ラムダデルタ卿には、決してギャラリーとしてだけお呼びしたのではない」
「そなたが妾と逆の目に張っているとお伝えしたら、卿はそなたの逆の目に張ると仰せになられた」
「…………………………あんた、まだ根に持ってるのね」
contexts.japanesePC: そなたが妾と逆の目に張っているとお伝えしたら、卿はそなたの逆の目に張ると仰せになられた。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「………ベアトも馬鹿ね。
この子はあんたのゲームであってもしっちゃかめっちゃかにするわよ」
「ラムダデルタ卿には、決してギャラリーとしてだけお呼びしたのではない」
「そなたが妾と逆の目に張っているとお伝えしたら、卿はそなたの逆の目に張ると仰せになられた」
「…………………………あんた、まだ根に持ってるのね」
contexts.WH: After informing me that you were betting against me, she said that she would bet against you."
contexts.MG:
"......You're dumb too, Beato.
If this kid's in your game, she'll make a mess of everything."
"I certainly didn't just bring Lady Lambdadelta here to watch from the sidelines.
After informing me that you were betting against me, she said that she would bet against you."
"............You're still holding a grudge, aren't you."
contexts.UP:
".........You're a fool too, Beato.
This kid won't make exceptions for your game, she'll turn everything into a preposterous farce."
"I didn't bring Lady Lambdadelta here solely to watch from the sidelines."
"After I informed her that you were betting against me, she said that she would bet against you."
"..............................You're still holding a grudge, aren't you."
contexts.note: MG retains the malformed perspective in After informing me that you were betting against me. UP correctly makes Beatrice the one who informed Lambdadelta.

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice tells Bern that after she informed Lambda of Bern betting against her, Lambda said she would bet against Bern.
findings.alternative: The translated latter clause correctly reports Lambda opposing Bern, but the initial recipient me reverses the information flow from Beatrice to Lambda.

findings.description: どういう勝敗になろうとも becomes No matter what issue we fight over.

contexts.japanese:
「…………こちらこそよろしくよ、ラムダ。
そしてベアト。
…どういう勝敗になろうとも、これは私たちにとってとても有意義な戦いになるわね」
contexts.japanesePC: 「…………こちらこそよろしくよ、ラムダ。そしてベアト。…どういう勝敗になろうとも、これは私たちにとってとても有意義な戦いになるわね。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「…………こちらこそよろしくよ、ラムダ。
そしてベアト。
…どういう勝敗になろうとも、これは私たちにとってとても有意義な戦いになるわね」
contexts.WH: "............I'll be counting on you, Lambda.  And Beato. ...No matter what issue we fight over, this will be a very significant battle for us."
contexts.MG:
"......I'll be counting on you, Lambda.
And you, Beato.
...No matter what we fight over, this will be a very significant battle for us all."
contexts.UP:
"............I look forward to it, Lambda.
And Beato.
...No matter who wins or who loses, this will be a very meaningful battle for us."
contexts.note: MG retains no matter what we fight over and changes battle outcome into subject matter. UP correctly says no matter who wins or loses.

findings.sourceReading: Bern says their battle will be meaningful regardless of how victory and defeat turn out.
findings.alternative: English retains general significance but shifts the variable from outcome to dispute topic.

findings.description: 私たちには勝敗以上に意義がある becomes who wins and who loses will be important.

contexts.japanese:
「そうね。
もちろん負ける気はないけど、私たちには勝敗以上に意義がある」
「何しろ妾たちは、退屈を愛さない」
contexts.japanesePC: 「そうね。もちろん負ける気はないけど、私たちには勝敗以上に意義がある。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「そうね。
もちろん負ける気はないけど、私たちには勝敗以上に意義がある」
「何しろ妾たちは、退屈を愛さない」
contexts.WH: "That's right.  Of course, I don't feel like losing, but who wins and who loses will be important."
contexts.MG:
"That's right.
Of course, I don't plan on losing, but we've got a goal beyond who wins and who loses."
"After all, we hate boredom."
contexts.UP:
"That's right.
Of course, I'm not gonna lose easy, but this is more important than winning and losing."
"After all, we have no love for boredom."
contexts.note: MG says they have a goal beyond victory; UP says the battle matters beyond victory. Neither retains the claim that who wins and loses is itself important.

findings.sourceReading: Lambda does not intend to lose, but agrees that the battle has significance beyond victory or defeat; Beatrice then identifies their shared hatred of boredom.
findings.alternative: 勝敗以上 acknowledges winning still matters, yet expressly locates greater significance beyond it, which English omits and instead emphasizes winning itself.

findings.description: 困ったことに is rendered Since when we are in trouble, making inference from moves dependent on being in trouble.

contexts.japanese:
困ったことに、相手の指し手から手の内を探ろうとしている私たちにとって、
これは非常に手ごわい情報のノイズ。
厄介な撹乱になりうるわ。
contexts.japanesePC: 困ったことに、相手の指し手から手の内を探ろうとしている私たちにとって、これは非常に手ごわい情報のノイズ。
contexts.japanesePS3:
困ったことに、相手の指し手から手の内を探ろうとしている私たちにとって、
これは非常に手ごわい情報のノイズ。
厄介な撹乱になりうるわ。
contexts.WH: Since when we are in trouble, we try to seek out our opponent's strategy by looking at their moves, this creates a very formidable amount of noise in our information.
contexts.MG:
Since, when we're in trouble, we try to seek out our opponent's strategy by looking at their moves,
this creates a very formidable amount of noise in our information.
That might cause a troublesome amount of disorder.
contexts.UP:
This is unfortunate for us, trying to seek out our opponent's strategy by looking at her moves,
because it creates a formidable amount of noise in our information.
This disorder could be troublesome.
contexts.note: MG retains the conditional framing; UP restores “This is unfortunate for us,” as an evaluation of the situation.

findings.sourceReading: Unfortunately for them, since they are trying to infer the opponent's strategy from her moves, intentionally suboptimal moves constitute formidable informational noise.
findings.alternative: The situation is troublesome, but the source is an evaluative introduction, not a when-clause restricting their method to troubled situations.

findings.description: 付け込ませたいかのように隙がある becomes One that makes me want to take advantage of it.

contexts.japanese:
…実は隙がある。
付け込ませたいかのように隙がある。
……それが罠なのか、こちらを試しているのかわからないけども。
contexts.japanesePC: 付け込ませたいかのように隙がある。
contexts.japanesePS3:
…実は隙がある。
付け込ませたいかのように隙がある。
……それが罠なのか、こちらを試しているのかわからないけども。
contexts.WH: One that makes me want to take advantage of it.
contexts.MG:
...there actually was a weak point.
A weak point that almost looks like she wanted you to take advantage of it.
...Though, I don't know if it's a trap or if she's testing us.
contexts.UP:
...there actually were weak points.
It looks almost as if she wants us to take advantage of them.
......Although, I don't know if it's a trap or if she's testing us.
contexts.note: Both editions say the gap makes the listener want to exploit it, rather than making Beatrice want exploitation.

findings.sourceReading: There is an opening as though Beatrice wants to let them exploit it. Bern does not know whether it is a trap or a test.
findings.alternative: Both suggest a tempting opening, but the causative source locates apparent intent with the one leaving the opening, while English explicitly makes Bern the person desiring exploitation.

findings.description: 魔女の戦いは守りが肝心よ becomes What is the most important element in defense during a witch's battle.

contexts.japanese:
魔女の戦いは守りが肝心よ？
勝とうとするより、負けないようにしなさい。
…認めたら負けなら、断じて認めては駄目。
contexts.japanesePC: 魔女の戦いは守りが肝心よ？
contexts.japanesePS3:
魔女の戦いは守りが肝心よ？
勝とうとするより、負けないようにしなさい。
…認めたら負けなら、断じて認めては駄目。
contexts.WH: What's the most important element in defense during a witch's battle?
contexts.MG:
What's the most important element in defense during a witch's battle?
Rather than trying to win, try not to lose.
...If accepting her means your defeat, then you definitely mustn't accept her.
contexts.UP:
Defense is crucial during a witch's battle, you know?
Rather than trying to win, try not to lose.
...If you lose when you accept her, then you definitely must not accept her.
contexts.note: MG retains the question about what matters in defense; UP states that defense itself is crucial.

findings.sourceReading: Bern states that defense is crucial in a witches' battle, then advises avoiding defeat rather than pursuing victory.
findings.alternative: A rhetorical question can introduce advice, but English asks for the key element within defense rather than asserting defense itself as the strategic priority.

contexts.japanese:
しかもあの子はあれでいて本当に負けず嫌いだから、
きっと今頃悔しくって歯軋りをして涙をぽろぽろ流してるわよ、
本当にざまぁないわよ、くすくす、ほーっほっほっほっほっほ！
contexts.japanesePC: しかもあの子はあれでいて本当に負けず嫌いだから、きっと今頃悔しくって歯軋りをして涙をぽろぽろ流してるわよ、本当にざまぁないわよ、くすくす、ほーっほっほっほっほっほ！
contexts.japanesePS3:

findings.sourceReading: Lambda says Bern is intensely averse to losing and imagines she is now grinding her teeth and crying in frustration.
findings.alternative: Lambda also bears a grudge, but the source subject is Bern's competitive disposition and conjectured current reaction, not Lambda's hatred and planned torment.

findings.description: 勝率を ... 絶対に近付けてやる becomes will associate myself just a tiny bit with you and your hopeless chances at winning.

contexts.japanese:
あんまり情けないから、ちょっとだけ力を貸してあげるわ。
この宇宙最強で絶対の魔女である大ラムダデルタ卿が、
あんたの絶望的な勝率を、ほんのちょっぴりだけ絶対に近付けてやるわ。
感謝なさい。
contexts.japanesePC: この宇宙最強で絶対の魔女である大ラムダデルタ卿が、あんたの絶望的な勝率を、ほんのちょっぴりだけ絶対に近付けてやるわ。感謝なさい。

あんまり情けないから、ちょっとだけ力を貸してあげるわ。
この宇宙最強で絶対の魔女である大ラムダデルタ卿が、
あんたの絶望的な勝率を、ほんのちょっぴりだけ絶対に近付けてやるわ。
感謝なさい。
contexts.WH: I, the great Lady Lambdadelta, the Witch of Certainty and the strongest in the universe, will associate myself just a tiny bit with you and your hopeless chances at winning.  You should thank me.
contexts.MG:
You're so pathetic, I'll help you just a little bit.
I, the great Lady Lambdadelta, the Witch of Certainty and the strongest in the universe,
will associate myself just a tiny bit with you and your hopeless chances at winning.
You should thank me.
contexts.UP:
You're so pathetic, I'll help you just a little bit.
I, the great Lady Lambdadelta, the Witch of Certainty and the strongest in the universe,
will bring your hopeless chances of winning just a teensy bit closer to certainty.
You better thank me.
contexts.note: MG retains association with hopeless chances; UP restores moving the listener’s chances closer to certainty.

findings.sourceReading: Lambda promises to move the reader's hopeless win probability a little closer to certainty through her power.
findings.alternative: English announces slight assistance in nearby lines, but substitutes affiliation for the specified operation on victory odds.

findings.description: 勝ちが見えると遊び出す becomes playing around by making it look like she has won.

contexts.japanese:
あの子はあと数手でチェックメイトできる局面を作りつつ、わざと詰めない。
下らない駒を取ったり、余計な駒を置いてより一方的な盤面にしてみたり。
早い話が、勝ちが見えると遊び出す悪い癖があるってわけ。
contexts.japanesePC: 早い話が、勝ちが見えると遊び出す悪い癖があるってわけ。
contexts.japanesePS3:
あの子はあと数手でチェックメイトできる局面を作りつつ、わざと詰めない。
下らない駒を取ったり、余計な駒を置いてより一方的な盤面にしてみたり。
早い話が、勝ちが見えると遊び出す悪い癖があるってわけ。
contexts.WH: In short, you could say she has the bad habit of playing around by making it look like she's won.
contexts.MG:
Though she'll set up the board in a way that'll let her win with just a few more moves, she'll intentionally avoid cornering you.
She'll do things like take worthless pieces and place excess pieces on the board to make things more one-sided.
Simply put, she's got the bad habit of playing around as soon as she thinks she's won.
contexts.UP:
That kid will make the board so she can win with just a few more moves, but she deliberately won't finish you off.
She'll do stuff like take worthless pieces, or put way too many pieces on the board to make things even more one‐sided.
The point is, she's got this bad habit of playing around when she thinks she's going to win.
contexts.note: Both editions restore imminent victory as the trigger for Beatrice’s wasteful play.

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice starts playing around once she sees victory ahead, instead of completing checkmate.
findings.alternative: The preceding English mentions a position a few moves from winning, but this sentence introduces making victory look apparent as the means of play rather than imminent victory triggering wasteful play.

findings.description: 妾の敗北に厚く張っておる continues the wagering metaphor and says Bernkastel has placed a heavy bet on Beatrice’s defeat. Push strongly for my defeat changes a wager into direct advocacy or effort.

contexts.japanese:
「隠し通せているつもりか。
そなたは人の領地まではるばるやって来て、妾の逆の目に張る不届き者よ。
妾のゲームを傍観するつもりでいて、妾の敗北に厚く張っておるのだろうが。
図星であろう…？」
contexts.japanesePC: 「隠し通せているつもりか。そなたは人の領地まで遥々やって来て、妾の逆目に張る不届き者よ。妾のゲームを傍観するつもりでいて、妾の敗北に厚く張っておるのだろうが。図星であろう…？」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「隠し通せているつもりか。
そなたは人の領地まではるばるやって来て、妾の逆の目に張る不届き者よ。
妾のゲームを傍観するつもりでいて、妾の敗北に厚く張っておるのだろうが。
図星であろう…？」
contexts.WH: "Were you planning on hiding it?  You're an outrageous person to come into someone else's territory from such a great distance and work against me.  You came to watch from the sidelines, and probably to push strongly for my defeat.  I've guessed right, haven't I...?"
contexts.MG:
"Were you planning on hiding it?
You're an outrageous person to come into someone else's territory from such a great distance to work against them.
You came to watch from the sidelines, and probably to push strongly for my defeat.
I've guessed right, haven't I...?"
contexts.UP:
"You thought you were hiding it?
How insolent, to travel all that way, and come into territory that isn't yours, just to bet against me.
You came here planning to watch my game from the sidelines, while having a large stake placed in my defeat.
I've guessed right, haven't I...?"
contexts.note: MG retains pushing strongly for Beatrice’s defeat. UP restores a large stake placed in her defeat and preserves the wagering frame.

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice accuses Bernkastel of entering another’s territory as a spectator while secretly betting heavily on Beatrice losing.
findings.alternative: Push for an outcome can loosely convey backing it strongly, and the previous phrase still mentions working against Beatrice.

findings.description: お敗れになられた stacks honorific forms around Lambdadelta’s defeat for conspicuous mock deference. You were defeated states the fact plainly and loses Beatrice’s exaggeratedly polite teasing.

contexts.japanese:
「そうと決まればベアト、さっそく作戦会議をするわよ！
その子の弱点は知り尽くしてる、それを全て伝授してあげるわ！」
「にもかかわらず、ラムダデルタ卿はお敗れになられた、と、くっくっくっく…！」
「もぉおおおぉ、教えたげない教えたげないッ！
ツーン！」
contexts.japanesePC: 「にもかかわらず、ラムダデルタ卿はお敗れになられた、と、くっくっくっく…！」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「そうと決まればベアト、さっそく作戦会議をするわよ！
その子の弱点は知り尽くしてる、それを全て伝授してあげるわ！」
「にもかかわらず、ラムダデルタ卿はお敗れになられた、と、くっくっくっく…！」
「もぉおおおぉ、教えたげない教えたげないッ！
ツーン！」
contexts.WH: "And yet, Lady Lambdadelta, you were defeated by her, *cackle*cackle*...!"
contexts.MG:
"If we're decided, Beato, then let's start a strategy meeting right now!
I know all of this girl's weak points, and I'll teach you all of them!"
"And yet, Lady Lambdadelta, you were defeated by her, *cackle*cackle*...!"
"Urrrrrrrrgggh, I won't tell you, I won't tell you!

"And yet, Lady Lambdadelta, you were defeated by her, I note... *cackle*cackle*...!"

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice responds to Lambdadelta’s claim of knowing every weakness by mock-politely noting that Lambdadelta nevertheless lost to Bernkastel.
findings.alternative: The formal title Lady and Beatrice’s cackle retain some teasing deference around the direct statement.

contexts.japanese:
……ベアトに看破されてしまったから白状する。
今のあなたは、かつてラムダの世界に囚われていた頃の私にそっくりなの。
過酷な運命の迷路に閉じ込められ、魔女にいいようにいたぶられている。
…私はそこから生まれた魔女。
……だからあなたの姉に当たるのかもしれない。
だからあなたに力を貸そうと決めたの。
contexts.japanesePC: 過酷な運命の迷路に閉じ込められ、魔女にいいようにいたぶられている。
contexts.japanesePS3:
……ベアトに看破されてしまったから白状する。
今のあなたは、かつてラムダの世界に囚われていた頃の私にそっくりなの。
過酷な運命の迷路に閉じ込められ、魔女にいいようにいたぶられている。

contexts.WH: Shut inside a labyrinth of cruel fate, tormented by a witch, in a manner of speaking.
contexts.MG:
...Beato saw through me, so I'll confess.
You are now just like I was in the past, when I was imprisoned inside Lambda's world.
Shut inside a labyrinth of cruel fate, tormented by a witch, in a manner of speaking.
...I am a witch who was born from there.
...So maybe I'm like an older sister to you.
So I decided that I'd lend you my power.

......Beato saw through me, so I'll confess.

...I am a witch who was born from there.
......So maybe I'm like an older sister to you.
